extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and novelists doing scene-level craft and revision
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist and diagnostic for crafting and revising individual scenes so they propel a novel forward; focuses on making each scene contain purpose, conflict, and consequences and on how scenes link into a causal chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Scene
rubrics_metrics.description: A story-building block that consists of a goal, the attempt to resolve that goal, and the resolution of that goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as the baseline definition: if a unit of text doesn't include a goal/attempt/resolution, it's not a scene but exposition, vignette, or dead weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Part Scene Test (Goal / Conflict / Stakes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene must contain: (1) Goal — the protagonist wants something (concrete, in this scene); (2) Conflict — something stands in the way; (3) Stakes — something bad will happen if they fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a scene lacks any of the three it isn't functioning as a scene. The goal should be concrete to the scene (not only long-term), conflict should meaningfully oppose that goal, and stakes must show real negative consequences of failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Red-Flag Question: 'Why is this here?'
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask of every scene: 'Why is this here?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the answer is 'because that's what happened' or 'because I wanted to show the character,' cut it or rebuild it around goal/conflict/stakes. Use this as a diagnostic to find filler scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Drive — Active Protagonist
rubrics_metrics.description: Drive comes from an active protagonist — pursuing a goal, not waiting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid passive protagonists who only react. Ensure the protagonist is making choices and taking actions that produce consequences and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Drive — Escalating Stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each scene should raise what is at risk; stakes should escalate across the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the cost of failure larger or more personal over time so tension increases; avoid scenes where stakes are flat or irrelevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Drive — Question Generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong drive makes the reader keep asking 'what now? what next?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design scenes and endings so they create unanswered questions that compel the reader forward (e.g., dilemmas, partial victories, new information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Drive — Causal Chain
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes should be causally connected: scene B is caused by scene A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure events follow from prior events (not random). Each scene's outcome should create the next scene's problem/goal; avoid drift or disconnected vignette sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Drive — Withheld Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Withholding information (so the reader senses something more) helps drive curiosity and forward motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategically reveal and hold back details to maintain questions and tension; don't withhold so much the reader is confused, but enough to compel turning pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene/Sequel Pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the scene/sequel alternation: Scene = goal → conflict → setback (or partial victory). Sequel = reaction → dilemma → decision (which sets the next scene's goal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pattern creates continuous forward motion: every scene leaves the protagonist in a worse or changed situation, and each sequel produces the new goal that drives the next scene. Use sequels for reaction and choices; use scenes for active attempts and obstacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Scene Failures (Anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent problems include: scenes without goals (filler); goals without conflict (easy victory); conflict without stakes (pointless); resolution that simply ends without setting up the next goal (drift); multiple parallel goals diluting drive; protagonist waiting for things to happen (passive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify these anti-patterns during revision and fix by adding/clarifying goal/conflict/stakes, consolidating or cutting parallel goals, and ensuring the protagonist acts rather than waits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Editing / Evaluative Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark every scene with its goal; identify the conflict; identify the stakes; identify the value shift (positive to negative or vice versa); check whether the next scene flows from this one's end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any checklist cell is empty, fix or cut. Additionally evaluate: Goal clearly present; Conflict clearly present; Stakes clearly present; Value shift accomplished; Causal connection to prior and next scene; Necessary to the larger story (would removing it break anything?); Forward momentum (reader wants to continue). Use these as explicit pass/fail checks when revising scenes.
